stories.title: Bill Koch's magnificent Aspen estate, originally listed at $125 million, now draws buyers with $33.515 million price tag
stories.summary: Billionaire Bill Koch's expansive Aspen estate has sold for $33.515 million after a luxury auction. The property, initially listed at $125 million, struggled to find a buyer for two years. After several price reductions, the 52-acre Elk Mountain Lodge went to a competitive bidding process. This sale highlights shifts in the ultra-luxury housing market and buyer selectivity. The transaction represents a notable luxury home sale in Aspen this year.

stories.title: Significant rock formation: 2.56 billion-year-old Pichhore granite discovered; offers clues to ancient geological processes
stories.summary: India's Pichhore orbicular granite, 2.56 billion years old, is a rare geological marvel. This ancient rock formation displays unusual spherical structures called orbicules, which are rarely found globally. Researchers discovered inherited zircon crystals indicating Earth's earliest crust recycled during the Neoarchean Era. The granite's formation suggests magma intrusion and rapid cooling deep beneath the surface. This significant find helps reconstruct conditions of the young Earth and early continents.

Landlord firm fined £42,500 after tenants found living among rats and human waste
stories.summary: A landlord company in County Durham has been fined £42,500 after tenants were found living in unsafe conditions, including sleeping among dead rats, mice, human waste and urine. The court heard the firm failed to carry out required property inspections and maintain valid gas safety certificates across several rental homes, prompting legal action by Durham County Council.

stories.title: Why people slept inside wooden cupboard beds for hundreds of years in medieval Europe
stories.summary: Box beds served as enclosed sleeping spaces in European homes for centuries. These wooden structures provided warmth during cold winters and saved limited living space. Families and workers shared these beds, sometimes leading to overcrowding concerns. As housing improved, box beds gradually disappeared from modern households. Modern versions now focus on privacy and design rather than necessity.
